criteria.revision: Open on the contrast rather than the raw fact: "From 3,300 feet up, Pidgeot can spot a splashing Magikarp—but when it hunts, it skims the water’s surface. What happens between those two views?" This uses the documented vision and water-skimming facts without claiming an unsupported dive sequence.

criteria.quote: "At that speed, Pidgeot skims water to hunt Magikarp."
criteria.revision: Remove the unsupported speed-to-waterline connection and make the concrete hunting detail do the work: "When hunting, Pidgeot skims the water’s surface to pick off unwary prey such as Magikarp."

criteria.quote: "What can Pidgeot do after spotting a Magikarp splash from that high?"
criteria.revision: Make the answer less immediately predictable and ground the mystery in the two documented perspectives: "It can see a splash from 3,300 feet—but why does its hunt end at the water’s surface?"

criteria.quote: "Pidgeot spots Magikarp from 3,300 feet." / "It notices the splash while already flying far overhead."
criteria.revision: Merge the first two scenes because they state the same vision fact. Use the freed scene to pivot from distant sight to the surprising low-water hunt: vision at 3,300 feet → Mach 2 flight → skimming the water to pick off Magikarp → feared talons.

criteria.quote: "Then it races through the sky at Mach 2."
criteria.revision: Hold back "Mach 2" until after the audience has absorbed the 3,300-foot sighting, then reveal it as a second distinct fact: "That would already be terrifying. Then the Pokédex adds this: Pidgeot flies at Mach 2 while seeking prey."

criteria.quote: "A SPLASH FROM 3,300 FEET" / "THE SPLASH GIVES IT AWAY"
criteria.revision: Cut or combine the repeated splash/vision scene. Give each remaining scene one unique idea: exceptional vision, Mach 2 prey-seeking flight, surface-skimming hunts for Magikarp, and feared talons.

criteria.quote: "Its vision finds the target, Mach 2 speed closes distance, and feared talons threaten at the waterline."
criteria.revision: Avoid presenting separate entries as one confirmed step-by-step attack. Replace with: "Pidgeot’s entries paint a hunter with impossible sight, Mach 2 flight, feared talons, and a habit of skimming water to pick off Magikarp."

criteria.quote: "Sky hunter or water hunter: which is scarier?"
criteria.revision: Ask viewers to choose between two documented, genuinely distinct details instead of implying Pidgeot is separately a water hunter: "Which is scarier: Pidgeot spotting a splashing Magikarp from 3,300 feet, or flying at Mach 2 while seeking prey?"
